title: Little brothers
hookLine: the friars minor, the lesser brothers

cards: Names for leaders tend to climb. Manager, senior manager, director, vice president, chief. Every title is a step up, and everyone can see who's where.

Francis's small band of followers needed a name. Some readers hear in his choice an echo of the Italian towns of his day, where, they say, the powerful were called the major people and everyone else the minor people.
Either way, Francis picked the low side, and he put it right in the name. Today's word: friar.

teach.b: Friar simply means brother. Francis's companions were the fratres minores: the lesser brothers, the little brothers. That's still the official name, the Order of Friars Minor.
His early biographer tells how it happened.
When the words of the rule were being written and they came to the phrase, let them be lesser, Francis said: I want this brotherhood to be called the Order of Lesser Brothers.
In the earliest rule the brothers kept, the idea runs all the way through.
Nobody is to be called prior, which means the one who comes first. All are lesser brothers, and they wash one another's feet. Even those put in charge are called ministers, which means servants.

teach.h: HE THAT IS THE LEADER, AS HE THAT SERVETH.
teach.b: The disciples argue about which of them is the greatest, and Jesus answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "But you not so: but he that is the greater among you, let him become as the younger; and he that is the leader, as he that serveth."
Friars are also a different shape of religious life from the monks who promise stability. They don't live behind a monastery wall for good.
They go out, into towns and along roads, among ordinary people, preaching, working, begging when they must.
Monks stay; friars move. The Church recognizes both as ways of giving a life to God. But a friar's whole identity starts from below: lesser, by choice, and brother, to everyone.

how: Franciscan friars call one another brother, and their superiors are called ministers and guardians rather than abbots or priors.

o: a brother in an order like Francis's, living among people
a church officer who collects alms for the poor
a monk who stays for life in one enclosed monastery

games.q: the lesser brothers — tap the pairs.

s: friars and monks are the same thing
monks promise stability in one house; friars go out into towns and along roads.
in Francis's earliest rule, no brother is to be called prior
all are lesser brothers, and they wash one another's feet.
the name friars minor was chosen without much thought
his early biographer says Francis heard 'let them be lesser' in the rule and chose the name on purpose.

games.q: your growing brotherhood needs a name, and the rule you're writing says 'let them be lesser.' what do you call yourselves?
o: the greater brothers, to earn respect.
games.why: Francis heard the rule say "let them be lesser" and named them the Order of Lesser Brothers, the friars minor.

practice: Think of one place where you usually take the higher seat, the one who decides, who speaks first, who's right, and without putting yourself down, picture standing there as a brother or sister instead of a boss.
Asking instead of telling, serving instead of directing, hearing out the person you'd usually overrule. If you pray, hold the gospel line: he that is the leader, as he that serveth.

wordCard.voice: Friar. Brother: a member of an order like Francis's lesser brothers, the friars minor, who live out among people rather than behind a monastery wall. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the lesser brothers, the official name of Francis's friars.

carryVoice: Your line: lesser brothers. Even the ones in charge are called servants. Same time tomorrow.
